dispatch: DIRECT Agent call, not Workflow — this is a pacer-spawned headless -p session, where the Workflow tool is review-gated (SKILL.md, retired-headless-degraded paragraph). One fable judgment seat, effort high, which is exactly the qa-verify.js taste-mode shape (ONE agent, no look stage).
brief_deviation: qa-verify.js's serverBrief and browseBrief are both browser/dev-server shaped and inapplicable to a terminal CLI. Substituted a CLI-shaped equivalent (run node bin/moon.js directly; evidence is captured stdout/stderr; no screenshots). Everything else — the taste rules, the severity vocabulary, the verdict vocabulary, the ten-uses requirement, the qa prompt_lines from the playbook — was passed verbatim.

flows_exercised: hemisphere inference via TZ (Sydney, Johannesburg, Kiritimati, UTC)

full-cycle art sweep k=0..1 waxing+waning, both hemispheres, via src/render.js — faketime is not installed and bin/moon.js calls new Date() with no env var or --date input, so the CLI itself can show exactly ONE dated moon per day

boredom_findings.what_gets_stale: Ten consecutive runs printed the byte-identical pair '░░░▓◗  30%  waxing crescent' / 'next full moon  28 Aug'. Nothing human-visible moves within a session, and near new/full the 5-cell art and whole-percent field will also be identical across consecutive DAYS. The only element guaranteed to differ tomorrow is the absolute date, which the user must do mental math against.
boredom_findings.suggestion: Append a relative countdown: 'next full moon  28 Aug (in 10 days)'.

boredom_findings.where: whole product, first-time user's second question
boredom_findings.what_gets_stale: The follow-up after the first reading — 'what will it be Friday?' — dead-ends. No --date flag, no env override, faketime absent, so exploration is impossible.
boredom_findings.suggestion: A --date <iso> flag reusing the existing astro path, still zero-dep.

boredom_findings.what_gets_stale: 'next full moon  28 Aug' dangles OUTSIDE and below the closed box at a 3-space indent that aligns with nothing in the frame. It reads like a row that fell out of the table, and it is the block's most interesting fact.
boredom_findings.suggestion: Make it a fourth detail row inside the frame.

boredom_findings.what_gets_stale: The one-liner's glyph ramp at low k is far steeper than the block's: 3% hairline, 8% reads as a half-lit edge, 18% reads near-quarter, while the block at the same k keeps a faithful thin arc. At k=0.004 the line shows an all-dark disc labeled 'waxing crescent 0%' while the block still draws a hairline — the two surfaces disagree about whether the moon is visible.
boredom_findings.suggestion: Hold the hairline glyph longer in lineArt, and let the low-k line borrow the block's hairline guard.
